title: Restore full pinned-MIT YEIS Places travel for stars, galaxies, and deep-sky landmarks

scope.subject: Native multi-scale Places navigation, dynamic galaxy detail, and deep-sky landmark rendering

research_summary: The current navigator restored MIT YEIS Search/Places but only star/system targets are first-class. The exact pinned MIT upstream already defines multi-scale navigation semantics: stars switch/open systems, galaxies use CameraController.goToPoint to arrive about 2.6 radii from the galaxy centre, and non-stellar landmarks arrive at 3.2 radii (5 radii for remnants). Upstream also dynamically maintains up to three GalaxyCloud renderers for galaxies within 18 radii, so travel to Andromeda/other galaxies does not collapse into an unresolved sprite. Deep-sky visibility is provided by LandmarkSprites, whose minimal code dependency closure is already mostly vendored; it adds landmarkImages metadata and approximately 1.5 MB of 15 licensed 512px photographs, while procedural billboards remain the base representation. Restore these upstream mechanisms rather than inventing a second spatial-navigation model.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT upstream implements goToGalaxy/goToLandmark with CameraController.goToPoint and dynamically keeps up to three GalaxyCloud instances for nearby galaxies.
Pinned MIT LandmarkSprites renders nebulae, clusters, remnants and record stars as real-position instanced billboards, with photograph atlas as progressive enhancement.
Pinned metadata identifies 15 512px deep-sky photographs as public domain NASA/ESA/STScI or CC BY 4.0 ESO/ESA-Hubble imagery and records per-image credits.
Pinned MIT Places catalogue already groups stars, galaxies, black holes, planets and deep-sky objects as curated destinations.

search_ladder.conclusion: The selected mother engine already contains the complete spatial navigation/rendering semantics; reuse the pinned implementation rather than another planetarium/navigation product.
The existing R3F-hosted YEIS scene can own upstream CameraController, GalaxyCloud and LandmarkSprites objects without a second canvas.
Restore upstream dynamic GalaxyCloud bookkeeping plus native goToPoint formulas and LandmarkSprites as one coherent Places subsystem.
LandmarkSprites and its small pinned photograph set cover deep-sky visuals; no new billboard/search/render package is needed.

coverage_matrix.capability: star/system destinations keep current Personal Universe Open semantics
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep product SystemScene entry for star-like targets; only spatial galaxy/landmark targets stay in native galactic view.

coverage_matrix.capability: galaxy travel remains visually resolved near arrival
coverage_matrix.decision: Restore upstream nearby-galaxy cloud lifecycle, not just goToPoint.

coverage_matrix.capability: non-stellar landmarks are visible and searchable at real coordinates
coverage_matrix.decision: Vendor pinned LandmarkSprites + metadata/photos and update it in the native frame loop.
All camera travel remains owned by pinned YEIS CameraController.
Keep code at e520568 MIT boundary and record each photograph source/license in project attribution.

candidates.name: Restore pinned MIT YEIS multi-scale Places travel + dynamic galaxy clouds + LandmarkSprites
candidates.license: MIT source at e520568; landmark photos public domain or CC BY 4.0 as recorded upstream
candidates.reason: Highest global coverage and lowest semantic risk: camera formulas, galaxy LOD lifecycle, landmark coordinates, renderer and curated Places all come from the already-selected mother engine.

candidates.name: Add goToPoint targets but keep one Milky Way cloud and no LandmarkSprites
candidates.source: Partial reuse of pinned camera formulas
candidates.reason: Creates destinations that can arrive at unresolved/blank near views; locally cheaper but globally incomplete.

candidates.name: Build a separate project-owned galaxy/landmark destination model and camera flight layer
candidates.reason: Duplicates coordinates, arrival heuristics and LOD behavior already present in YEIS and creates two spatial authorities.

decision.rationale: Restore the pinned MIT YEIS navigation and rendering mechanisms as a coherent subsystem. Personal Universe continues to own product-phase semantics and content presentation, while YEIS remains the single authority for spatial coordinates, camera travel, galaxy LOD and deep-sky landmark rendering.
decision.fallback: If photo assets prove too costly, keep the exact LandmarkSprites procedural billboard path and disable only the photograph atlas; do not remove landmark coordinates or native travel.
